card: Updates the p2p_eviction functional test to ensure it actually exercises block-time protection logic during peer eviction. Currently, the test connects block-sending peers first, allowing fallback connection-time protection to shield them from eviction even if block-time protection is disabled. Connecting the block-sending peers last ensures that the test fails if block-time eviction protection regresses. No external dependencies exist.
evidence: Author demonstrates that deleting the block-sending call on master allows the test to pass anyway because connection-time fallback protects the same peers: 'This can be shown by deleting the line where the peers send their block (L71 on master)' (PR description).
Author notes: 'With this change the test fails if the CompareNodeBlockTime protection in SelectNodeToEvict is removed' (commit c75cdce1f9).
problem: The functional test for node eviction passes even if block-time protection is omitted or broken. Because the test currently connects the block-sending peers first, fallback eviction logic protects them anyway as the oldest connections, hiding regressions in block-time protection.

risk.why: Only modifies functional test code, potentially causing CI test failures if incorrect.

scope_notes: Small test reordering change in a single functional test file.
summary: Fixes a false positive in the peer eviction functional test by connecting block-sending peers last instead of first. This ensures test coverage specifically asserts peer protection based on recent novel block transmissions rather than fallback connection-age protection.
